walkthrough: Goal: paint with brushes that leave a shape, not only a round line: a chalky textured edge for loose painting, a flat chisel for blocky concept-art strokes, a rough opaque paint, and a spray of speckles for texture; every stroke looks the same at every zoom, after undo and redo and after reopening.

Entry: open OpenPaint on the tablet (2880 x 1800, landscape) on an empty library; the pen draws with the Ink Pen. Tap the Brush button: the panel lists the brushes by job, each with a stroke it painted: Pencil, Ink Pen, Inker, Monoline, Hard Round, Soft Brush, then the four new ones Textured Round, Flat, Opaque Paint and Speckle, then StreamLine.

Textured Round: tap it and paint a long stroke with rising pressure. The stroke reads as a soft-edged, hand-painted chalk mark: its edge is broken and grainy, the grain inside is fixed to the canvas, and the chalk shape tumbles a little along the stroke; no dotted line shows. Pressure widens it and lays more paint.

Flat: tap it and paint a stroke that turns a corner. The tip is a thin flat chisel held across the stroke: the stroke is wide with clean square ends, and through the turn the chisel follows the direction of the hand, so the band keeps its width. Pressure lays more paint; where it crosses itself it never darkens.

Opaque Paint: tap it and paint a stroke. A rough square tip follows the direction, overlapping densely: a solid band with a rough, bristly edge and blocky ends, like thick paint; pressure lays more paint.

Speckle: tap it and draw a stroke over empty canvas. Small dots of different sizes are sprayed around the path, up to three radii away from it; where dots overlap they build up. Undo it, add a layer, and draw the same stroke again: the same speckles land in the same places (the dots follow the stroke's own seed, fixed here; on the tablet every stroke gets its own).
Undo and redo take a stroke away and bring it back exactly; a stamped stroke is one step like any other.

Symmetry: Actions > Canvas > Drawing Guide, Radial; close Actions; paint a Textured Round stroke: it appears eight times, mirrored, each copy with the same chalk pattern mirrored (copies keep the stroke's seed); one undo step takes all eight.
Zoom: pinch to about 4x: once the fingers rest the stamps sharpen; the chalk's broken edge and the chisel's square ends stay one screen pixel sharp, not blurred or blocky.
Failure and cancel: nothing new can fail; a dot (a tap) leaves one stamp; the Ink Pen, Inker, Pencil and every older stroke draw exactly as before.
Reopen: leave the app and come back: every stroke, speckle and copy is exactly as left.
